title: MIHVER M0 RequirementSpec
description: The compiled, typed set of requirements Requirement Derivation produces from one eligible IntentSpec version, per docs/contracts/REQUIREMENT_SPEC.md (ADR-0003, Status: Proposed). Failed compilation produces no RequirementSpec -- there is no 'failed' status value here, mirroring intent-spec.schema.json's identical 'Failed parsing produces no IntentSpec' decision (see docs/contracts/REQUIREMENT_SPEC_SCHEMA_MAPPING.md's 'Failed-outcome serialization decision'). Semantic references and cross-artifact invariants are additionally checked by the deterministic contract validator against a required companion IntentSpec, and an optional companion MemoryContext wherever an R-24 memory-informed rationale is cited.

consumed_intent_spec.description: The exact IntentSpec version this RequirementSpec version compiles. Never RequirementSpec's own prior version -- see 'IntentSpec Supersession Effects'.

revision.description: Required non-null whenever version > 1 (validator-enforced); required null at version 1, since there is nothing to revise yet.

status.description: R-16/R-21. Never 'failed' -- Failed means no RequirementSpec artifact exists at all, per this schema's own top-level description.

requirements.description: R-17: an empty array is a valid Complete output when the consumed IntentSpec genuinely supports no formal Requirements.

open_items.description: Carried-forward unresolved items this version does not, or must not, resolve -- unresolved Ambiguities/Conflicts, Unknowns that fail R-19's fillability test, R-19-eligible Unknowns left deliberately unfilled, and R-20 unresolved constraint-candidates.

memoryContextEntryRef.description: The stable (memory_context_id, entry_id) pair MEMORY_CONTEXT_SCHEMA_MAPPING.md's 'Stable identity for cross-artifact reference' establishes. Used only for an R-24 memory-informed rationale -- never as a Requirement-Level Inference premise (see requirementLevelInferencePremise's closed oneOf, which structurally forecloses this shape, R-23).

trigger.description: One of REQUIREMENT_SPEC.md's 'Requirement Identity and Versioning' named reasons -- never an unexplained change of judgment or a stylistic rewrite.

affected_requirement_ids.description: Validator-enforced: at least one of affected_requirement_ids/affected_open_item_ids must be non-empty -- a revision that affects nothing is not a revision.

provenanceRef.description: R-01: a reference into the specific consumed IntentSpec version -- never into this RequirementSpec itself, and never a MemoryContext reference (memory is never ordinary provenance, R-24).

source_open_item_id.description: R-19/R-09: the surviving Unknown in the consumed IntentSpec this default fills. Validator-checked to resolve to an open_item of kind 'unknown' -- never 'ambiguity', and never an ID this RequirementSpec manufactures itself.

rationale.description: R-09/R-19: Requirement Derivation's own independent justification that this value is a defensible internal implementation/measurement detail -- never 'because memory said so' (see memory_informed_rationale below, which is additional, never a substitute).

memory_informed_rationale.description: R-24: present only when a MemoryContext entry informed this value. Additional to, never a replacement for, 'rationale' above -- the validator requires both when this is non-null.

testability.description: R-21. This layer records the structural shape of a satisfaction procedure; it does not itself execute, prove, or validate the procedure's substantive correctness for any real candidate -- see REQUIREMENT_SPEC_SCHEMA_MAPPING.md's 'Complete/Partial representation' for exactly what is, and is not, enforced.

oneOf.description: A plain SATISFIED/NOT_SATISFIED procedure, fully determined by the clause's own recorded content -- no INDETERMINATE branch needed or offered.

grounding_open_item_id.description: R-21 condition 1: the surviving Unknown routing a candidate to INDETERMINATE. Validator-checked to resolve to an open_item of kind 'unknown' in the consumed IntentSpec -- never 'ambiguity' or 'conflict', which R-21 condition 1 categorically excludes from this branch.

admissible_readings.description: R-21 condition 2: the closed, IntentSpec-grounded reading domain. Structural presence (at least two readings) is schema-enforced; whether these readings are genuinely grounded in the IntentSpec's own recorded content -- as opposed to a domain Requirement Derivation invented after the fact -- is Not enforceable at this layer, since intent-spec.schema.json's own 'unknown' shape carries no structured candidate-reading field to check against (only 'ambiguity' does).

oneOf.description: Testability-blocked: no faithful procedure -- not even one with an INDETERMINATE branch -- can be written from this clause's own recorded content.

strength.description: R-05/R-06: force -> strength, one-directional, non-inflationary. Validator-checked against the mapped strength of every basis Claim's own force in the companion IntentSpec.

basis.description: R-01: the normative basis -- one or more Claims whose own force this clause's strength is mapped from (R-02: never a force-absent descriptive Claim; the validator checks this). Deliberately claim-only, not the open_item_id generality R-01's provenance text also allows for a Requirement overall: an Open Item carries no force to map a strength from, so it can never legitimately be a clause's normative basis. A surviving Open Item's two legitimate roles are structurally elsewhere -- filling a detail within an already-settled clause (working_defaults.source_open_item_id) or grounding a clause's own INDETERMINATE testability branch (testability.grounding_open_item_id) -- never as if it were itself a strength source.

rationale_refs.description: R-02: non-normative rationale, structurally distinct from 'basis'. May cite a force-absent descriptive Claim -- removing this array must leave the clause's normative content completely unchanged.

scope_condition.description: R-07: a preserved, formal condition -- never a manufactured biconditional. Required whenever any basis Claim itself carries a scope_condition (validator-enforced structurally; faithful preservation of the condition's exact meaning is Not enforceable at this layer).

origins.description: The set of distinct origins among this clause's basis Claim(s) -- validator-checked to equal that set exactly, never independently asserted. Deliberately a set, not a single scalar: 'Requirement Cardinality and Granularity' permits several Claims of DIFFERENT origins to jointly define one testable behavior (e.g. a User-Provided obligation corroborated by an Inferred one), and 'Information-Loss Rules' forbids collapsing that distinction into one summary value -- a single-origin clause is simply the common case of this same array holding one element.

derivation_confidences.description: The set of distinct derivation_confidence values among this clause's Inferred-origin basis Claim(s). Required whenever 'inferred' is a member of origins (mirroring those Claims' own derivation_confidence values, never collapsed to one); forbidden otherwise.

working_defaults.description: R-09/R-19/R-24: zero or more Requirement-Derivation-introduced value fills for an internal implementation/measurement detail within this already-settled clause.

requirementLevelInferencePremise.description: R-10/R-23: only an accepted IntentSpec Claim, or an already-derived Requirement (or one specific clause of it) in this same RequirementSpec -- never a MemoryContext entry. This closed oneOf makes R-23 structurally impossible, not merely discouraged: there is no fourth shape here for a memory reference to occupy. 'requirement' is R-10's own literal premise unit (a whole Requirement), validator-checked to have a single strength across all its clauses -- undefined otherwise. 'requirement_clause' is the narrower escape valve for a mixed-strength combined Requirement, letting an inference cite one specific clause so R-22's strength inheritance is always deterministic even when the whole Requirement has no single strength -- a representation refinement of 'Requirement Cardinality and Granularity's already-established per-clause strength independence, not a new semantic rule, and additive to 'requirement' rather than a replacement for it (see REQUIREMENT_SPEC_SCHEMA_MAPPING.md).

strength.description: R-22: must exactly equal the premise's own strength -- never independently chosen, strengthened, or weakened. Validator-enforced.

reasoning.description: R-10: the stated technical/operational-implication reasoning -- never an interpretive judgment about what the user meant.

scope_condition.description: R-07: required whenever the premise itself carries a scope_condition (validator-enforced structurally), so a condition preserved through a direct-compilation clause is not silently dropped one inference-step later.

requirementLevelInferenceClause.description: R-22 forbids a derivation_confidence field here by construction -- this shape has none, unlike directCompilationClause's Inferred-origin case, which is a distinct concept (IntentSpec's own Inference confidence, not this stage's).

settled_rationale.description: Required when provisional is false (validator-enforced) -- 'Requirement Derivation may instead record it as settled only when it states why continued reconsideration isn't warranted... silence is not that statement.' Forbidden when provisional is true.

clauses.description: R-15: one or more clauses. Multiple clauses may carry different strengths within one Requirement (mixed-strength combination, 'Requirement Cardinality and Granularity') -- strength is never homogenized across them.

invalidation.description: R-14: required non-null when status is 'invalidated'; required null when 'valid'. An invalidated Requirement is never deleted -- it remains in this version's historical record.

source_open_item_id.description: Resolves to an 'ambiguity'-kind open item in the consumed IntentSpec. R-08: never resolved by Requirement Derivation, at any Decision Impact level.

source_conflict_id.description: Resolves to a Conflict in the consumed IntentSpec. R-08: never resolved by Requirement Derivation.

source_open_item_id.description: Resolves to an 'unknown'-kind open item in the consumed IntentSpec that fails R-19's fillability test -- treated exactly as an Ambiguity or Conflict, regardless of its formal Unknown classification.

An R-19-eligible Unknown Requirement Derivation chose not to fill this version, carried forward instead. Does not, by itself, make any area Partial -- see Case 25; only a clause whose own testability structurally depends on it does.

source_claim_id.description: R-20: a Claim whose binding/constraining content is evident but whose own force never resolved to obligation/prohibition/permission/preference. Never assigned a manufactured strength.
